title: Daily carry-over credits stored energy at the peak price while the next day's native replay inherits that energy, so a plan that just holds a full battery shows a saving
label: bug
steps:
1. As owner, open /sites/6d4db49bf87e/savings (This month).
2. Read the 8 Nov row and the levers.
3. Read the per-day rows read-only from savings_days in companies/6321e32a-...db (db.py). Compare Karachi 2 Nov with 3 Nov.
expected: A kWh left in the battery at day end should be credited at what it is worth to the arm that would otherwise have it. Each day's native replay starts from the actual's measured state of charge, so the native arm then spends that energy itself the next day. The two days together should equal a continuous replay: the energy's value counted once.
actual:
The carry-over uses v_end = 0.95 × the day's highest import price − wear = Rs 27.19/kWh in November (Rs 40.02 peak). Next morning the native arm starts with that energy and self-use spends it off-peak (worth 0.95 × 26.98 − 10.83 ≈ Rs 14.8/kWh). Each kWh of end-of-day gap is over-credited by about Rs 12.4.
- Faisalabad 8 Nov: the whole month's claim of Rs 1,901 is carry-over +4,384 (204.25 kWh actual against 43.0 kWh native at day end), wear +1,666 and off-peak −4,149. The actual discharged 0.8 kWh and the native 154.57 kWh. Peak import was identical (384.74 kWh), so the native used its stored solar off-peak. A two-day continuous calculation gives about Rs 1,900 less than the per-day ledger for each night the battery is held full. The site is now in 'hold' at 95%.
- Karachi 2 Nov: +4,748 is mostly carry-over +5,792 (286.4 against 73.36 kWh). On 3 Nov the native replay starts at 286.4, discharges 153.33 kWh after midnight at the off-peak rate and stops at its 125 kWh backup floor. The native got about Rs 4,010 of value from energy the ledger had credited at Rs 5,792 (about Rs 1,780 over-credit).
evidence:
API 8 Nov (Faisalabad): levers {peak_window 0, offpeak_energy −4149, wear 1666, carry_over 4384}, saving 1901.13.
DB rows: FSD 2026-11-08 eA 204.25 eN 43.0 v 27.19 dis 0.8/154.57 pkimp 384.74/384.74; KHI 2026-11-02 eA 286.4 eN 73.36 carry 5791.8; KHI 2026-11-03 native dis 153.33 eN 125.0.
Code: verify.py:641-645 (both replays start at the actual's soc0), 669-675 (c_next = max(c_imp), v_end), 733 (carry). Spec Part 8.2 prices carry-over only at switchback block boundaries.

title: Off-grid farm claims Rs 12,581 this month (Rs 21,349 over 12 days) while burning more diesel than its native settings; the claim is all carry-over
label: bug
steps:
1. As owner, open /sites/47895916bed4/savings (This month).
2. Compare the 'Saving against the native settings' card, the 'Diesel saved' card and the 'Carry-over' lever.
3. Call GET /api/sites/47895916bed4/savings?start=2026-10-01&end=2026-11-09.
expected: At a site whose only running cost is diesel (plus wear), a saving should come with litres saved. Stored energy should be valued at the fuel it actually displaces. Customers see this per-day ledger, and it drives the fee check.
actual:
- November: saving Rs 12,581, of which carry-over is Rs 9,244 (73%), wear Rs 2,839 and genset Rs 497. Diesel saved is −0.3 L.
- 28 Oct–8 Nov: claimed Rs 21,349. Carry-over is +30,046, genset −13,972, and 34.6 L more diesel was burnt.
- The actual arm burnt more fuel than native on 7 of 12 days and ended the day higher than native on 11 of 12.
- v_end is Rs 152–163/kWh: the genset's all-in average cost at its night load ratio (about 0.34), including no-load burn and Rs 400/h run-hour cost. The set runs 10–20 h a day, so a stored kWh mostly displaces genset output at the margin: fuel slope 0.273 L × Rs ~400 + O&M 8 → 0.95 × 117.4 − 10.83 ≈ Rs 101/kWh. Valued that way, the 12-day carry-over falls from about 30.0k to about 19.3k.
- The fee check reads Rs 47,178 a month (one third Rs 15,726) on this basis.
evidence:
API (native baseline, 1 Oct–9 Nov): levers {genset −13971.53, wear 5275.26, carry_over 30045.63}, litres_saved −34.6.
DB v_end 151.61–163.19.
The page shows 'Diesel saved −0.3 L' beside 'Rs 12,581'.
DESIGN_LOG 2026-11-07 Round 5 'Open: the per-day carry-over at off-grid sites is noisy... Customers see the per-day ledger, so this matters before a pilot'.
Code: verify.py:669-675.

title: The MDI lever changes with the chosen date range: one day can claim a whole month's MDI, and unscored days in the month are ignored
label: spec-mismatch
steps:
1. As owner, open /sites/e9941b41c70b/savings, choose Custom, and set From and To to 3 Nov 2026.
2. Repeat for 1–3 Nov and for This month.
3. Call GET /api/sites/6d4db49bf87e/savings?start=2026-10-01&end=2026-10-31 and compare its MDI month with /telemetry/days for October.
expected: Spec Part 8.2: MDI is the month's single highest block, so the lever comes from the full-month counterfactual and is the same whatever sub-range is viewed. The month's peak must include every day of the billing month, including observation and unscored days. A one-day view should not book a month's demand charge.
actual:
- Karachi 3 Nov alone: 'Saving against the native settings Rs 41,099'. The day lost Rs 1,526, and MDI +42,625 comes from that day's 839 against 873 kW. The month's real peak so far is 902 kW.
- 1–3 Nov shows Rs 53,336, more than the whole month to date (Rs 43,594).
- 8 Nov alone shows −Rs 20,415.
- 'Last 30 days' shows Rs 90,112: two months of MDI (Rs 94,088) from 12 scored days, whose daily sum is −Rs 3,975.
- Faisalabad October: MDI −Rs 30,275 (328.45 actual against 304.23 baseline, from 28–31 Oct only). October's billed MDI was 337.06 kW, set on 26 Oct, a native observation day, so both arms' October demand is 337.06 kW and the true lever is 0.
- The fee check follows these numbers: Faisalabad 28 Oct alone gives Rs 173,741 a month.
evidence:
API (start/end): KHI 11-03 claimed 41099.29, mdi 42625, months {'2026-11': 838.57/872.67}; KHI 11-01..11-03 claimed 53336.09; KHI 11-08 −20414.97; FSD Oct mdi −30275 {328.45, 304.23}.
Telemetry days: FSD 2026-10-26 peak 337.06 (not in savings_days).
Code: verify.py:1047-1066 (months built only from the rows inside [d0,d1]).

title: Legacy net-metering agreement end date is ignored: exports stay priced at the import rate after expiry instead of the net-billing rate (Rs 8.13)
label: bug
area: Tariff vectors and bill rebuild: prosumer regime
steps:
1. As owner, call GET /api/sites/37b2fd882dcb/prices?day=2026-12-24. The Lahore mall's agreement_end is 2026-12-23.
2. Call GET /api/sites/f014f039638b/prices ('AUDIT api expired agreement', agreement_end 2025-01-01).
expected: R9 8.3 and SRO 547(I)/2026: a legacy agreement keeps its terms only until it expires. After agreement_end the connection is billed under net billing: exports credited at NAEPP (Rs 8.13 in the library), imports at the TOU rate. The optimiser, the prices page, the ledger and the bill rebuild should all switch on that date.
actual:
- Lahore 24 Dec 2026 and 1 Feb 2027: c_exp is 38.95 and 47.75, the same as before expiry.
- The audit site whose agreement ended on 1 Jan 2025 still exports at 26.97/40.01 on 9 Nov 2026.
- agreement_start and agreement_end are read only by an alert ('The net metering legacy agreement ends on 2026-12-23'). Pricing ignores them.
- An optimiser seeing about 5× the real export value would plan battery and PV exports at peak, and the export lever would be credited at the import rate.
evidence:
API: lhr 2026-12-24 c_exp [38.95, 47.75]; f014f039638b c_exp [26.97, 40.01] with agreement_end 2025-01-01.
Code: the only use of the dates is alerts.py:155-163. tariffs.py:701, 723-745 (vectors) and 548-553, 607-611 (rebuild) branch on regime only.

title: Month-to-date saving books the whole month's MDI reduction while the daily cost of holding it builds up, overstating Karachi's month
label: ux
steps:
1. As owner, open /sites/e9941b41c70b/savings (This month, 1–9 Nov).
2. Read the headline, the MDI lever and the daily bars.
expected: A month-to-date figure that a CFO can believe: either a full-month MDI lever set against a full month of the costs that achieve it, or the lever shown as provisional or spread over the month.
actual:
- Headline Rs 43,594, of which MDI is Rs 41,638 (33 kW × Rs 1,250), booked in full after 8 days. Every day without an outage loses money: 3–8 Nov average −Rs 1,713 a day. The plan cycles 240–420 kWh a day to hold the 902 kW cap; peak +9.2–11.5k, off-peak −7.4–8.8k, wear −2.6–4.6k.
- If the remaining 22 days look like 3–8 Nov with no outage, the month ends near +Rs 5,900, not Rs 43,594.
- The fee check (Rs 37,508 a month) and the headline both lean on this front-loaded credit. A 1 MW plant's 'perfect' bound is Rs 615 on the same page.

title: The 'perfect-foresight upper bound' is below the claimed saving and even negative, so it is not a bound
label: bug
steps:
1. As owner, open /sites/e9941b41c70b/savings and read 'Perfect-foresight bound'.
2. Open /sites/37b2fd882dcb/savings.
3. Choose Custom 3–3 Nov on Karachi.
expected: Spec 8.2: a hindsight re-solve reported as the upper bound ('not achievable, for reference'). It should be at least the realised saving and never below about zero against native, measured on the same levers (MDI included) and the same 1-minute basis.
actual:
- Karachi November: bound Rs 615 against a claim of Rs 43,594.
- Karachi 3 Nov: bound −Rs 3,121 against a claim of +Rs 41,099.
- Lahore (monitor, actual equals native): bound −Rs 7,314, including −6,327.77 on 6 Nov and −1,816.93 on 1 Nov.
- Causes:
  - The bound's cost (energy + genset + wear − terminal) leaves out the MDI it pays to cap; the hindsight solve takes the day's month-to-date M0.
  - It solves at 15 minutes but is compared with the native arm priced per minute.
  - It has a 5 s limit.
- These days were computed 14:41–14:44 UTC on 8 Nov, before the audit load, so load does not explain them.
evidence:
API native perfect_foresight_rs: KHI Nov 615.12; LHR Nov −7314. DB per day: KHI 11-04 −4883.2, 11-03 −3120.93; LHR 11-06 −6327.77.
Code: verify.py:771-810 (cost excludes the MDI value; time_limit=5.0).

title: Connection tax flags and the ICP baseline cannot be set in the web app; every site is priced as a GST-registered filer with no ICP
label: feature-gap
steps:
1. As owner, open Add a site (or Site settings), connection tab.
2. Look for GST recoverable, s.235 adjustable, STRN/ATL, and the ICP eligibility and baselines by month and period.
3. Call GET /api/sites/<any>: tax.gst_recoverable is true and icp.eligible is false everywhere.
expected: Spec Part 3 'connections': ICP baseline by month and period, and tax flags gst_recoverable, s235_adjustable, STRN and ATL. Spec Part 6: the wizard's tariff tab captures them from a bill. An ICP-eligible B-2 or B-3 site above its baseline is priced at Rs 22.98 + positive FCA instead of 26.98/40.02. A site without STRN, or a domestic or agricultural one, pays 18% GST plus 3% further tax on every rupee.
actual:
- The form edits only the province.
- site-form.ts:187 says 'the fields this form does not edit (ICP baseline, tax flags, seasonal multiplier) are kept from the saved connection'.
- The backend defaults all flags to True (sites.py:103) and icp.eligible to false.
- The bearable-cost basis, the optimiser's prices and every saving therefore assume a registered, ATL industrial filer with no ICP. This is wrong for the very sites (B-2/B-3 with growth) the brief targets, and silently 18–21% low for non-recoverable sites.
evidence: grep in frontend/src: no gst_recoverable, s235 or icp input. site-form.ts:187, 207. sites.py:103. tariffs.py:475, 484. Spec EMS_BUILD_PLAN.md lines 227, 563.

title: The 'tuned' baseline can be worse than native: Lahore's tuned table costs Rs 294 a day more than the native settings
label: spec-mismatch
steps:
1. As owner, open /sites/37b2fd882dcb/savings and read 'Saving, tuned' in the days table.
2. Read the tuned rows in savings_days read-only.
expected: Spec 8.1: the tuned baseline is the best static table the engine can fit, and claims must beat it. It should never be worse than the native capture, so the candidates must include a native-like self-use table, and the fit should value end-of-day energy as the ledger does.
actual:
- On 9 of 12 days the tuned table costs +Rs 293.77 more than actual (which equals native at this monitor site). Every day it discharges 57 kWh at peak (+2,752), recharges off-peak (−2,078), pays wear (−617.5) and ends 10 kWh lower (−350).
- On A-2(c) the spread (48.28 against 39.48 / 0.9025) is below wear (Rs 10.83/kWh), so it loses money.
- All 8 TUNED_VARIANTS force a peak 'discharge' row and none is plain self-use.
- fit_tuned prices candidates with v_end = 0, so draining the battery looks free.
evidence:
DB tuned rows LHR: levers {peak_window −2752.13, offpeak_energy 2078.05, wear 617.5, carry_over 350.35} → 293.77, on 1–5, 7 and 8 Nov, plus 30–31 Oct at 299.56–299.57.
Code: verify.py:541-555 (TUNED_VARIANTS, tuned_table); verify.py:600-604 (price_arm(..., 0.0)).

title: A genset day before the first entered diesel price is silently priced at a later price
label: bug
steps:
1. As owner, open Faisalabad savings for 28–29 Oct.
2. Divide the genset lever, less the start, run-hour and O&M costs, by litres_native.
expected: A day with no price on or before it is flagged ('no fuel price for this day') or uses the latest earlier price. It does not borrow a future price without saying so.
actual:
- The first HSD price is valid from 30 Oct (Rs 400.67).
- 29 Oct's genset lever of Rs 20,644 for 43.71 L implies about Rs 400.7/L, so it borrowed 30 Oct's price. tariffs.fuel_price falls back to the earliest row of any date.
- The genset lever carries no flag for this.
evidence:
DB FSD 2026-10-29 litres native 43.71, genset lever 20644. /api/tariffs/fuel: first hsd valid_from 2026-10-30.
Code: tariffs.py:299-301.
